hook: Literary analysis in 1978 matched detective Sherlock Holmes against Count Dracula.

sections.voiceover: Literary analysis in 1978 matched detective Sherlock Holmes against Count Dracula.
sections.visual_cue: Archival print showing Victorian London street with high-contrast lighting.
sections.sfx_cue: Low bass drone with paper turning sound.

sections.voiceover: In The Sussex Vampire, Sherlock Holmes investigated a client believing in supernatural forces. Where did literary analysts track Count Dracula?
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of vintage Arthur Conan Doyle story text alongside publisher archive documents.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft clock ticking sound and fountain pen writing.
b_roll: Penguin Random House archival book display

sections.voiceover: However, Sherlockian.net documented Holmes investigating a case where the client believed the supernatural was involved.
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing magnifying glass over detective notes and dark gothic silhouette graphics.
b_roll: Magnifying glass macro shot on text

sections.voiceover: In August 1978, Phoebe-Lou Adams reviewed the matchup in The Atlantic. Penguin Random House cataloged the dossier under ISBN 9781789099287.
sections.visual_cue: Sequence showing Atlantic publication banner, academic journal cover, and ISBN catalog card.
sections.sfx_cue: Camera shutter click followed by rising orchestral chord.

sections.voiceover: Don't miss Christian Klaver's Sherlock Holmes and Count Dracula from Penguin Random House.
